paper.core_task: Evaluating motion utilization in video MLLMs for referring video segmentation

contributions.name: A motion-centric probing and evaluation framework for video segmentation
contributions.author_claim_text: we provide a study of the ability of video MLLMs in utilizing motion information within language-guided video segmentation. Towards the latter, we create a motion-centric probing and evaluation technique
contributions.description: A framework that uses a static keyframe paired with a dynamic video to test whether video MLLMs truly use motion cues or are misled by static information in referring video segmentation.

contributions.name: Strong static and semi-temporal baselines for referring video segmentation
contributions.author_claim_text: we propose three strong baselines that outperform the state of the art while being static biased.
contributions.description: Three baselines using MLLMs and SAM/SAM 2.0 that rely on static or semi-temporal information, yet achieve state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks.

contributions.name: Analysis of motion referring expression properties
contributions.author_claim_text: we propose quantitative means to analyze the properties existing in referring expressions that can drive better evaluation for the use of motion beyond a single image.
contributions.description: An analysis using GPT-4o to categorize motion referring expressions into dynamic and static groups based on properties like multi-step actions and static cues.

novelty_claims.text: The proposed baseline—using an MLLM to identify keyframes and perform grounding, followed by SAM 2 for propagation—lacks technical novelty.
The evaluation technique for referring video segmentation based on keyframe selection is unique.
